content.text: This clearly shows the errors are PaymentProviderFailed 503s from api.io-pay.example, which per the service register is io-pay, a third-party dependency owned by IO Payments Ltd. No changes/deploys occurred. This matches upstream-dependency-failure.

hypotheses.subject: io-pay
hypotheses.summary: io-shop's account page calls api.io-pay.example (io-pay) synchronously to render, and starting at 22:06:00Z that dependency began returning 503s on the card endpoint, driving error rate from baseline to 100% within a couple of minutes. No deploy or config change occurred on io-shop in the hours before onset, and the rollout is converged on a single revision, ruling out internal causes.

supporting_evidence.claim: PaymentProviderFailed: api.io-pay.example returned 503 for /v1/shoppers/shopper-3815-1-0/card at src/io_shop/payment_provider.py:95
account page error rate at 100.00% over the last minute
io-pay: third-party, owned by IO Payments Ltd, at api.io-pay.example - Holds the card Io charges. Called while the account page renders
Deployment of io-shop has converged: all 3 replicas are running the same revision.

hypotheses.subject: io-pay
hypotheses.summary: If io-pay were instead considered an internal system, the same 503 pattern would point to an internal dependency failure, but the service register explicitly marks io-pay as third-party/owned by IO Payments Ltd, making this less likely than the upstream explanation.

supporting_evidence.claim: io-pay: third-party, owned by IO Payments Ltd, at api.io-pay.example
